queries: WITH t AS (SELECT CustomerId, SUM(Total) AS total FROM Invoice GROUP BY CustomerId), s AS (SELECT CustomerId, total, total * 1.0 / SUM(total) OVER () AS share FROM t), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s), k AS (SELECT s.total, s.share, a.avg_share FROM s CROSS JOIN a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share) SELECT AVG(total) AS avg_spent, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_avg_share FROM k

assumptions.assumption: Only customers with at least one invoice are counted. The average share is taken over those customers, so it equals 1 divided by their count.
The 'average share' is the plain mean of the per-customer shares. 'Beats the average share' means share minus that mean, averaged over the kept customers.

alternatives.interpretation: Customers with no invoices are included with a total of 0 and a share of 0. This lowers the average share, so more customers may qualify.
alternatives.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT c.CustomerId, COALESCE(SUM(i.Total), 0) AS total FROM Customer c LEFT JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId), s AS (SELECT CustomerId, total, total * 1.0 / SUM(total) OVER () AS share FROM t), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s), k AS (SELECT s.total, s.share, a.avg_share FROM s CROSS JOIN a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share) SELECT AVG(total) AS avg_spent, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_avg_share FROM k

assumptions.assumption: The average share is taken over customers who have at least one invoice. Customers with no invoices are not counted as zero-spend customers.
The share is a decimal fraction (0 to 1) of the sum of all invoice totals. The result is not rounded.
The 'average share' to beat is the mean of all customers' shares. The two output averages are taken over the kept customers only.

alternatives.interpretation: Every customer in the Customer table counts, including those with no invoices, who get a total of 0. This lowers the average share.
alternatives.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT c.CustomerId, COALESCE(SUM(i.Total), 0) AS total FROM Customer c LEFT JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId), s AS (SELECT CustomerId, total, total * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(total) FROM t) AS share FROM t), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT AVG(s.total) AS avg_spent, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_share_excess FROM s CROSS JOIN a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share;

assumptions.assumption: Customers are those with at least one invoice. Customers with no invoices are left out of the share average. The average share is the mean of per-customer shares across those customers.
The output's average share is the mean share of the kept customers (above-average ones), not the overall average share used as the cutoff.

alternatives.interpretation: Include every customer in the Customer table, counting customers with no invoices as total 0. This lowers the average share to 1 divided by the number of all customers.
